sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Franklin County, KY?
sections.html:
It depends on where the house sits. Everyone in Franklin County gets a county bill from the Franklin County Sheriff. Owners inside the City of Frankfort get a second bill from the city's Finance Office, which also collects for Frankfort Independent Schools.

The Franklin County PVA values the property and sits at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, in Frankfort, with a phone line at (502) 875-8780 and hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. The sheriff's office moved to the Public Safety Complex at 974 River Bend Road and answers at (502) 875-8740. Its website has a tax bill search with online payment, and a secure drop box sits at the front door.

The city bill uses the same PVA values, which Frankfort describes as 100 percent of fair market value on January 1. Questions about the value, an exemption or a mailing address go to the PVA, not to the city.

sections.h2: How do the county and Frankfort tax deadlines compare?
sections.html:
They differ. The county bill follows the statewide timetable in KRS 134.015, while the city sets its own calendar. A Frankfort homeowner should read both bills, because a discount window that works for one can already be closed for the other.

Franklin County sheriff bill versus City of Frankfort bill (sources: KRS 134.015, City of Frankfort Finance Office)
ItemCounty billCity of Frankfort bill
Discount2 percent if paid in full by November 12 percent on payments received before November 30
Due without penaltyThrough December 31By December 31
Late charge5 percent in January, 10 percent after January 3110 percent plus interest after the due date
Where to paySheriff, 974 River Bend Road, or onlineCity Finance Office, (502) 875-8500, or online

Frankfort says city bills are available by November 1 and can be searched and paid through its online property tax portal. If your lender pays from escrow, it is the owner's job to get each bill to the servicer.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Franklin County itself?
sections.html:
Franklin County holds the state capital. It was formed in 1795 from parts of Woodford, Mercer and Shelby counties and covers 208 square miles of land. The county's six neighbors are Owen, Scott, Woodford, Anderson, Shelby and Henry, and the Frankfort micropolitan area is built around the city.

Roads include Interstate 64, US 60, US 127, US 421, US 460 and KY 676. Two school systems serve the county: Franklin County Public Schools, which covers most of the area including much of Frankfort, and Frankfort Independent Schools, which takes in downtown, South Frankfort near the Capitol, and Bellepoint. Kentucky State University and parks such as Josephine Sculpture Park and the Fort Hill woodland trails add to what buyers look at.

  • Estimated population in 2025: 52,649, up 2.1 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $216,600.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 64.5 percent, so about a third of homes are rentals.
  • Median gross rent: $967.
  • Median household income: $65,298, with 12.3 percent of people in poverty.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 96.

About 73 percent of residents lived in urban areas in 2020, which is unusual for a Kentucky county. That gives sellers in Frankfort a wider pool of buyers than in most rural counties, and values that make the tax bill larger in dollar terms.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Franklin County assessment?
sections.html:
You begin at the PVA, since Kentucky does not let an owner appeal until a conference has happened. The Department of Revenue says the tax roll must be open to the public for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, and the PVA has to run a notice about it in the county's largest newspaper.

After the conference, file the appeal with the county clerk by the close of business on the day after inspection ends. The local board of assessment appeals then convenes 25 to 35 days later, and it hears only evidence presented with both you and the PVA in the room. Bring concrete proof, such as comparable sales, a recent appraisal, repair estimates or insurance records. A board must explain in writing any change it makes, and you may record the hearing.

Most appeals finish before bills print. If the final value ends up above the figure you claimed, the clerk issues a supplemental bill for the difference.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Franklin County?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled. The state figure is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and it comes off the assessed value before the rate is applied. On a house valued at the county median of $216,600, the taxable assessment falls to $167,500.

You apply through the Franklin County PVA. Ask the PVA how ownership on the January 1 assessment date affects a buyer who closes later in the year. A seller should tell the PVA after the sale so the exemption leaves the old address.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Franklin County taxes when I sell?
sections.html:
They stay attached to the property. Under KRS 134.015, a delinquent bill is the owner's personal debt as of the assessment date, and the resulting lien follows the parcel through any sale until the taxes are paid or the lien period runs out.

Bills still open after April 15 go from the sheriff to the county clerk. Each month adds 1 percent interest, and a clerk's commission of 10 percent applies. If the county attorney has mailed a first notice, a 20 percent attorney commission is added too.

  • Request the current payoff from the sheriff at (502) 875-8740, and from the Finance Office at (502) 875-8500 if the home is inside Frankfort.
  • Pay both bills at closing so the title company can issue a clear policy.
  • If a delinquent house also needs repairs, a cash purchase that closes as-is can settle the taxes out of the sale price without a listing period.

faqs.q: Do I pay both the county and the city in Frankfort?
faqs.a: Yes. A home inside Frankfort receives a county bill collected by the sheriff and a city bill collected by the City of Frankfort Finance Office, which also covers Frankfort Independent Schools.

faqs.q: Where is the Franklin County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office is at 974 River Bend Road in Frankfort, KY 40601, and the phone is (502) 875-8740. You can also search and pay a bill on the sheriff's website.

faqs.q: Where is the Franklin County PVA?
faqs.a: It is at 313 West Main Street, 2nd Floor, Room 209, Frankfort, KY 40601. Call (502) 875-8780. Hours listed by the county are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the homestead exemption amount in Franklin County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It applies to owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and you file with the PVA.

faqs.q: How soon can Franklin County taxes lead to a tax sale?
faqs.a: Not before the April 15 transfer to the clerk. The sale must then be set between 90 and 135 days later, and the county attorney sends notices before it happens.
